# #189 round-2 delta: PASS-WITH-NOTES

Head: `26d2df93dba7bb02dbaf7829928875c52d8961b3`

Delta against `703cde7710d62080907527de0e426e3d2fbe5c26` and reviewer output `d00b9fdf7672d7525f8900d59f80428ad83d4e65`. **F001 is closed. No new correctness blocker found.**

## Atomic veto

`crates/store/src/idle_nudges.rs:40-46,142-160` now uses one conditional `INSERT OR IGNORE ... SELECT`. It requires an existing Idle, untombstoned seat and no qualifying own event after the supplied anchor. Both checks run inside the inserting statement under `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`; another writer cannot change those facts between the predicate and insert/commit. Only a positive inserted-row count authorizes the send.

`mark_then_nudge` returns nothing on a veto. The controlled-race regression reads a due stretch, then independently changes its own event, state or tombstone. Each case asserts no mark, nudge or FYI. The existing stable-stretch test remains a positive control, including restart and re-arming. This closes the required mark-time race; it is not a promise that no activity can occur after commit and before physical delivery.

## Other delta changes

- The newest-own read and veto use the same predicate as migration 0046, explicitly selecting `spine_own_events`. Reports count; idle activity, malformed activity JSON and pushed messages do not. `CASE WHEN json_valid` prevents malformed activity payloads from breaking index maintenance. The newest event is found behind 2000 idle rows; an idle-only seat returns none.
- Candidate traversal is holder-driven through a registry-snapshot map, replacing vector membership. Background eligibility now seeks live jobs by owner instead of loading global pending-work rows. Missing/busy/tombstoned snapshot seats are spared; read failures still log and skip.
- FYI collision handling reads the existing `(origin, id)` row in the same write transaction. A different sender **or** recipient appends `fyi.refused` on the intended recipient and preserves the old row. Delivery observes that event and returns `E-RS-FYI-ID-TAKEN`, not a held receipt. The native HTTP hold routes the error through the shared failure handler, so it cannot become `ok:true`.
- Sixteen OS-random bytes are minted before the mark. An RNG error marks nothing. The occurrence is used in both the nudge and prime-FYI IDs; once-per-stretch identity remains the persisted mark, not the random string.
- Plan-222 ordering and suppression, normal-versus-held delivery, rendered labels and prime selection are unchanged. Migration 0046 remains consistent with schema version 46.

## Notes and proof ceiling

**N001:** the same-recipient/different-sender FYI conflict is implemented but not executed by the new test. The test covers same sender/different recipient, plus the same-sender/same-recipient retry. A mutation removing only the sender comparison would survive. This half was source-reviewed; add a focused sender-only conflict regression in the next approved test batch.

**N002:** duplicate-anchor insert-loser behavior remains source-inspected. Sequential/restart tests stop at the pre-check; the newly executed `false` results are freshness/liveness vetoes, not duplicate insert contention. The primary key and inserted-row check are correct by inspection. A focused duplicate mark or two-contender case would complete that proof. Marks still record at most one attempt, not guaranteed delivery after a crash; failed sends are intentionally not retried.

Other predictable daemon notice IDs remain outside this occurrence-randomization change, as disclosed in the PR. The shared FYI collision refusal prevents false held success for them but does not guarantee their notice arrives; normal-message IDs are not protected by that FYI guard.

**Cost:** no new loop, timer, poll or launch. The existing 60-second round now has O(S+H) snapshot/holder preparation, one indexed own-event lookup and mark lookup per eligible idle holder, and an owner-job seek only after the age/mark checks. Due holders add queue/holdings/claims reads and one mark transaction with a seat-key and own-event range seek. Notification cost is one holder attempt plus one FYI per distinct selected prime. Index construction is a one-time migration cost. Live before/after measurements remain the performance owner's proof, not inferred from this CI.

No local reviewer-owned build, test, dependency installation or live probe was run. No product or canonical plan state was edited.
